components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The editor's primary action: brand-600 fill, white Medium 14px, 4px corners, 32px tall.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 32px; padding: 0 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 4px; background: oklch(0.505 0.085 185); color: #fff; font: 500 14px/1 "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease-out, scale 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.42 0.07 185); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px oklch(0.6 0.095 185); } .ds-btn-primary:active { scale: 0.97; }

components.description: Secondary editor action: hairline on the background, hover muted.

narrative.overview:
raseeda is a local-first invoice generator: no accounts, no servers, no tracking, all data in the browser's IndexedDB. The interface should feel like a precise, trustworthy document tool, closer to a spreadsheet or a design canvas than to a consumer landing page. The invoice being edited is the loudest thing on screen: a sheet of white A4 paper lying on a grey desk, surrounded by quiet chrome.

The visual language is deliberately quiet around that sheet. Chrome is achromatic, the brand accent is a single deep-teal ramp, radii are small, and controls are compact. The paper itself never changes with the app theme, because it is a preview of the PDF that gets downloaded.

The marketing homepage is light and airy: a warm off-white canvas, warm near-black ink, a pale teal-blue sky with drifting clouds over the real editor, and pale pastel washes behind short loops of the editor at work. It shows the product rather than describing it. Ink carries the actions, teal marks the brand's own column and ticks, and one dark violet panel, the open source terminal, is the named exception.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral chrome; colour is reserved for the brand accent and for status.
One accent: the deep-teal `brand` ramp carries every emphasis (one named exception on the homepage).
White paper on a grey desk: the invoice page previews the PDF exactly.
Tight geometry in the editor: 3px surfaces, 4px controls, 32px default control height, 13px control text.
The editor has its own neutral chrome (plain greys, a near-black or near-white primary) and a light/dark switch; the rest of the site is light.
The homepage is rounder and softer: pills, 12 to 32px corners, rings instead of borders, the real editor in every picture.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The teal `brand` ramp is the only accent. Never introduce a second hue for emphasis; status colours are for status only, the homepage's tile hues mark content only, and the night panel is the one recorded exception.

rules.name: The Terminal Exception Rule
rules.body: The Run your own copy panel is a dark `zinc-950` surface lit by violet, indigo and magenta lights, with a violet band running round its terminal. It is deliberate and approved, and it stays inside that one panel: violet appears nowhere else on the site except as the keyword colour in the code tiles.

rules.name: The Ink Action Rule
rules.body: Homepage actions are ink, not teal: the primary action is a solid `ink` pill and secondary actions are frosted white pills. Teal on the homepage marks and hovers; it never fills a button there.

rules.name: The 600 Fill Rule
rules.body: Solid brand fills under white text are `brand-600` or darker. `brand-500` is for rings, switches and borders.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: The invoice page is white paper with dark ink in every app theme, because it previews the printed PDF. Anything drawn on the page uses `paper-*` tokens (or the brand wash for edit affordances), never chrome roles or raw Tailwind greys or blues.

rules.name: The Token Rule
rules.body: Brand colour comes from the `brand-*` ramp, never raw Tailwind `blue-*`, `teal-*` or hex, so the next change of hue stays a change to `globals.css` and the icons.

rules.name: The Dark Mode Honesty Rule
rules.body: Only the editor has a dark mode. The `/create` route sets `data-editor-theme` (and `.dark` when dark) on `<html>` before first paint and clears it on the way out, and the `html[data-editor-theme]` blocks in `globals.css` redefine the chrome roles for it (light: panels `#fcfcfc`, desk `#f6f6f6`; dark: panels `#161616`, desk `#121212`). The page (`[data-paper]`) takes the light roles back in both themes, and `dark:` utilities skip it. The homepage and privacy page stay light; do not claim dark mode for them.

rules.name: The Role Rule
rules.body: Homepage and privacy-page text takes its size and leading from a `lib/type-scale.ts` role through `typeClass()`; `.home-type` re-sets the role variables at marketing values. Pick a role, never a hand-written size.

rules.name: The 13px Control Rule
rules.body: Dense editor controls are 13px; buttons stay 14px Medium and meta drops to 12px. The homepage's pictures of the editor mirror 13px so they read as the product.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is above the page". In-flow cards, rows, and panels get a hairline, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Ring Rule
rules.body: On the homepage, containers are outlined with a 1px ring, never a border plus shadow: `zinc-950` at 5% around tiles, at 10% around white cards, the comparison table, question groups and menus; `white` at 5% around the night panel.

dos: Do reference semantic roles (`bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border-border`) in app chrome so retheming stays possible.
Do use `paper-*` tokens for everything drawn on the invoice page, and `brand-50` plus `brand-500` for its edit affordances.
Do put solid brand fills on `brand-600` (hover `brand-700`) and keep `brand-500` for focus rings and borders.
Do keep the A4 page free of responsive breakpoints; scale it with zoom.
Do give coarse pointers 44px targets with `pointer-coarse:` variants.
Do separate stacked and adjacent surfaces with `flex` or `grid` plus `gap-*` (use `gap-px` on a coloured parent for hairlines).
Do stay on `rounded-surface` / `rounded-control`, the 32px control height and 13px control text for editor chrome.
Do reach for `shadow-menu` for floating chrome rather than picking raw shadow utilities per component.
Do tint destructive actions; reserve solid saturated fills for the brand.
Do mirror any new PDF colour as a literal hex in the renderer and record it in the PDF palette here.
Do use the one `CreateInvoiceLink` ink pill for the homepage's primary action, with a soft pill beside it for the secondary one.
Do size homepage text with a type role through `typeClass()`.
Do show the product on the homepage with the editor's own pieces under `data-editor-chrome`, in Geist at the editor's sizes, or with real PDF renders.
Do give each homepage tile its own pair of `TILE_HUES` so neighbours never match.
Do run looping homepage motion only while it is on screen, in CSS on transforms and opacity, and hold it still or at its end state under reduced motion.
Do prove privacy claims with something the visitor can check (the real lines of code, links to them) rather than decorative ticks.
donts: Don't use `space-y-*`, `space-x-*`, `divide-x`, or `divide-y` (breaks with conditional and fragment children; owner-controlled `gap` is the rule).
Don't put white text on `brand-500` or lighter; it fails AA.
Don't put brand teal on the PDF.
Don't let the invoice page follow the app theme or use chrome roles, raw `zinc-*`/`blue-*`/`teal-*`, or responsive classes.
Don't hard-code hex or raw greys in editor chrome; hex belongs to the PDF renderer and the editor theme blocks in `globals.css`.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or bring back the coral accent the rename brief proposed; the night panel's violet is the one recorded exception and stays inside that panel.
Don't fill a homepage button with teal, or use a tile hue for an action or a link.
Don't reach for heavy or black shadows; prefer a hairline border or ring, and keep any shadow soft and neutral.
